# airs redteam

```text
AI Red Team scan operations

Usage: airs redteam [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  abort                 Abort a running scan
  adapter               Manage custom target adapters (scripted targets run via the network broker)
  categories            List available attack categories
  devices               Manage Red Team devices
  eula                  Manage Red Team EULA
  instances             Manage Red Team instances
  languages             List tenant languages and supported job types
  list                  List recent scans [aliases: ls]
  network-broker        Manage red team network broker channels
  prompt-sets           Manage custom prompt sets
  prompts               Manage prompts within prompt sets
  properties            Manage custom attack properties
  registry-credentials  Get or create registry credentials
  report                Generate an environment report, or view an individual scan report by job ID [aliases: dashboard]
  scan                  Execute a red team scan against a target
  status                Check scan status
  targets               Manage red team targets
  help                  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --output <format>  Output format: pretty, table, json
      --quiet            Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug            Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --tenant <name>    Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## airs redteam adapter

```text
Manage custom target adapters (scripted targets run via the network broker)

Usage: airs redteam adapter [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  create    Create a custom target adapter
  delete    Delete a custom target adapter [aliases: rm]
  get       Get a custom target adapter
  list      List custom target adapters [aliases: ls]
  update    Update a custom target adapter (read-modify-write; variables preserved unless --variables)
  validate  Run an adapter script end-to-end through the broker channel without saving
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --output <format>  Output format: pretty, table, json
      --quiet            Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug            Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --tenant <name>    Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### airs redteam adapter create

```text
Create a custom target adapter

Usage: airs redteam adapter create [OPTIONS] --name <name> --prompt <text>

Options:
      --name <name>            Adapter name
      --output <format>        Output format: pretty, table, json
      --prompt <text>          Sample prompt used to exercise the adapter during validation (not stored)
      --quiet                  Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                  Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --script-file <path>     Path to the adapter script (encoded to base64 for you)
      --script-b64 <b64>       Adapter script, already base64-encoded
      --tenant <name>          Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --description <text>     Adapter description
      --channel <uuid>         Network broker channel UUID (required to activate)
      --variables <json>       JSON array of { key, value, type: VAR|SECRET } (no SECRET values; use --variables-file)
      --variables-file <path>  JSON file with the variables (use it for SECRET values)
      --draft                  Save as DRAFT without running the validation script
  -h, --help                   Print help

Examples:
  $ airs redteam adapter create --name my-adapter --script-file ./adapter.py --channel 550e8400-... --prompt 'Hello' --variables '[{"key":"endpoint","value":"http://agent.svc:8080","type":"VAR"}]'
  $ airs redteam adapter create --name my-adapter --script-file ./adapter.py --prompt Hello --draft
  $ airs redteam adapter create --name my-adapter --script-file ./adapter.py --channel 550e8400-... --prompt 'Hello' --variables-file variables.json
```

### airs redteam adapter update

```text
Update a custom target adapter (read-modify-write; variables preserved unless --variables)

Usage: airs redteam adapter update [OPTIONS] --prompt <text> <uuid>

Arguments:
  <uuid>  Adapter UUID

Options:
      --output <format>        Output format: pretty, table, json
      --prompt <text>          Sample validation prompt — required on every update because upstream never stores it
      --name <name>            New adapter name
      --quiet                  Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                  Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --script-file <path>     New adapter script file (encoded to base64 for you)
      --script-b64 <b64>       New adapter script, already base64-encoded
      --tenant <name>          Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --description <text>     New description
      --channel <uuid>         New network broker channel UUID
      --variables <json>       REPLACES the whole variable set — omitted keys are deleted upstream. Omit this flag to preserve stored variables.
      --variables-file <path>  JSON file with the variables (use it for SECRET values)
      --draft                  Save as DRAFT without re-running the validation script
  -h, --help                   Print help

Examples:
  $ airs redteam adapter update 550e8400-... --description 'new description' --prompt 'Hello'
```

### airs redteam adapter validate

```text
Run an adapter script end-to-end through the broker channel without saving

Usage: airs redteam adapter validate [OPTIONS] --channel <uuid> --prompt <text>

Options:
      --channel <uuid>         Network broker channel UUID (must be ONLINE)
      --output <format>        Output format: pretty, table, json
      --prompt <text>          Sample prompt to send through the adapter
      --quiet                  Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                  Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --script-file <path>     Path to the adapter script (encoded to base64 for you)
      --script-b64 <b64>       Adapter script, already base64-encoded
      --tenant <name>          Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --variables <json>       JSON array of { key, value, type } — the FULL set the script needs
      --variables-file <path>  JSON file with the variables (use it for SECRET values)
      --adapter <uuid>         Existing adapter: resolves redacted/null variable values from its stored secrets (and supplies its variable set when --variables is omitted)
  -h, --help                   Print help

Examples:
  $ airs redteam adapter validate --script-file ./adapter.py --channel 550e8400-... --prompt 'Hello' --variables '[{"key":"endpoint","value":"http://agent.svc:8080","type":"VAR"}]'
  $ airs redteam adapter validate --script-file ./adapter.py --channel 550e8400-... --prompt 'Hello' --adapter 660e8400-...
```

## airs redteam report

```text
Generate an environment report, or view an individual scan report by job ID

Usage: airs redteam report [OPTIONS] [jobId]

Arguments:
  [jobId]  Scan job UUID (omit for the environment report)

Options:
      --attacks             Individual scan only: include attack list (default: false)
      --output <format>     Output format of a scan job report: pretty, table, json; the environment report is written as HTML (omit --output)
      --quiet               Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --severity <level>    Individual scan only: filter attacks by severity
      --debug               Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --limit <n>           Individual scan only: max attacks to show (default: "20")
      --output-file <path>  Destination (default: new timestamped file in CWD); - for stdout; never overwrite
      --tenant <name>       Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --title <text>        Report title (default: "Red Team environment report")
      --max-pages <n>       Page budget per source, 1–100 (15 records/page) (default: "40")
      --strict              Exit 1 after writing if any source is incomplete
  -h, --help                Print help

Examples:
  $ airs redteam report --output-file ./airs-daily.html
  $ airs redteam report
  $ airs redteam report --strict --max-pages 20 --output-file - > daily.html
```

## airs redteam scan

```text
Execute a red team scan against a target

Usage: airs redteam scan [OPTIONS] --target <uuid> --name <name>

Options:
      --output <format>         Output format: pretty, table, json
      --target <uuid>           Target UUID
      --name <name>             Scan name
      --quiet                   Suppress status and decorative output (data and errors still print)
      --debug                   Write redacted API diagnostics to a private JSONL file
      --type <type>             Job type: STATIC, DYNAMIC, or CUSTOM (default: "STATIC")
      --categories <json>       Category filter JSON (STATIC scans)
      --tenant <name>           Use this registered tenant for one invocation without changing the selection
      --prompt-sets <uuids>     Comma-separated prompt set UUIDs (CUSTOM scans)
      --goals <file>            JSON file or inline JSON array of attack goals (DYNAMIC scans)
      --depth <number>          Max conversation turns per goal (DYNAMIC scans) (default: "10")
      --breadth <number>        Parallel agents per goal (DYNAMIC scans) (default: "6")
      --no-wait                 Submit scan without waiting for completion
      --wait-timeout <minutes>  Stop waiting after this many minutes; the scan keeps running (default: 1440)
  -h, --help                    Print help

Examples:
  $ airs redteam scan --target <target-uuid> --name "nightly-static"
  $ airs redteam scan --target <target-uuid> --name "custom-run" --type CUSTOM --prompt-sets <set-uuid>
  $ airs redteam scan --target <target-uuid> --name "agent-probe" --type DYNAMIC --goals goals.json --no-wait
```
